english.title: Give false unsworn evidence as a witness in criminal proceedings which if sworn would have amounted to perjury

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Youth Justice and Criminal Evidence Act 1999

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) wilfully gave false unsworn evidence as a witness at criminal proceedings at which you were giving evidence pursuant to section 56(2) or (3) of the Youth Justice and Criminal Evidence Act 1999 and which, had it been sworn, would have amounted to perjury in that you gave such evidence, being material to those proceedings, knowing it to be false or did not believe it to be true
english.legislation: Contrary to section 57(2) and (3) of the Youth Justice and Criminal Evidence Act 1999.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
gave false evidence as a witness
knowing that evidence
to be false / not believing it to be true

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See Section 55 for determining whether a witness should be sworn
(ii) Where the defendant is under the age of fourteen the penalty is a fine not exceeding 250 (two hundred and fifty pounds)

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding £1000 (one thousand pounds)

Time limit for prosecutions
six months
